Don't get me wrong, I love this game! It was a staple of my childhood, helped to get people interested in wolves and learn about them, and I am currently perfecting it (79% of the way there!). The reason I don't recommend WQ: Classic is because of how far the game has come since; Classic is vastly inferior to Anniversary Edition. [b]Many cons in Classic are improved or nonexistent in AE, which will be in bold.[/b] I only recommend this to those who are wanting a taste of nostalgia or to 100% their potential favorite childhood game.

[h1]Pros[/h1]
[list]
[*]You will get Classic for free automatically if you buy Anniversary Edition, and I believe the reverse is also true.
[*]Educational, and education typically gets people interested in conservation.
[*]Nostalgic. I'm sure many people made many good memories on here, not to mention the old game aesthetic.
[*]Since support for this game has ended, all DLCs are now available for free in the base game.
[*]They removed multiplayer related Steam achievements since multiplayer servers were unfortunately shut down, to not frustrate Steam achievement hunters. You can still see them in the in-game achievement menu, however.
[/list]

[h1]Cons[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]The controls are a bit strange (Q to sprint? Shift to sneak?), especially the camera. You can't strafe and use A and D to turn your wolf and the camera. There's no mouse control for the camera unless you have it enabled to steer your wolf, you need to press 9 and 0 to make the camera orbit.[/b]
[*][b]The NPCs are kinda dumb and don't act very realistically. The social encounter arena in Amethyst Mountain is very basic, using dialog instead of emotes to communicate and fight with the NPC. Weak elk flee immediately while strong ones stand their ground, instead of the whole herd standing their ground together before stampeding. Pups cannot hide in the den unless you leave.[/b]
[*][b]Balancing is weird. Hunger and health are the same stat for some reason, and along with stamina, will slow you down if it gets low. I'm not sure if it's just because of the stats I have on my wolf, but stamina won't drain just from running, however it drains extremely fast when you latch onto prey such that you will need to sit/lay down to regain stamina and continue hunting. This is both annoying gameplay and unrealistic, wolves are persistent hunters which means they have a lot of stamina compared to their prey in order to chase and hunt continuously for a long time and tire out their prey.[/b]
[*][b]Wolf territories and elk herds are static circles on the map and wolves and elk herds will only spawn within those circles. For wolves, only one at a time will exist, typically close to the middle of the territory. Elk herds can move around after spawning and will migrate for as long as they're loaded in.[/b]
[*][b]Multiplayer servers have been shut down and the developers haven't given us tools to host our own servers.[/b]
[*][b]Some grindy "kill X amount of Y" type achievements, and the ones for surviving with one pup seem kinda redundant/excessive/unnecessary?[/b]
[/list]

A Once-Great Game, Left Behind.

WolfQuest was a groundbreaking and heartfelt experience when it first released. It offered something rare: the chance to step into the life of a wild wolf, hunt, survive, raise a family, and connect with others through multiplayer. For many players — especially on mobile and PC — it became more than just a game. It became a lasting memory.

The developers have explained that old code dating back to 2007 made it difficult to continue supporting the classic version. But even with that explanation, it doesn’t change how it feels: the original loyal players were still left behind. Multiplayer was removed, updates stopped, and no real preservation effort was made to honor what the community had built.

It’s disappointing not because people stopped caring about WolfQuest, but because it feels like the developers stopped caring about us.
Mobile players especially have been left with a broken, unsupported experience despite their support and love for the game.

WolfQuest didn’t die because players moved on.
It faded because it was allowed to fade without real care for the players who helped it thrive.

I will always appreciate what WolfQuest meant to me — but I can’t ignore the sadness of how it was handled in the end.
Players, old and new, deserve better.

We still notice. We still remember. WolfQuest deserved better.
